texts: mixed: two things leave the translator guessing here. Bare capitalized 'Keepers' is a shape it cannot decide -- proper name or plain role word, and whether sentence 5's 'Keepers' are the same people (it built two unrelated groups) -- so write 'the keepers' in both places if it is one crew. And 'had relit' is a past perfect whose only event to precede sits in a different sentence, which the parse left unordered here while ordering the parallel 'had yielded' in sentence 10; 'On day 17 of Year 1, the keepers relit the eleven lanterns of the Middle Row.' avoids that inconsistency if nothing turns on the relighting coming first.
good. the eleven lanterns are carried over from sentence 1 and the dim burning is handed to each lantern by a per-member rule, exactly as a predicate on a definite plural should be.

bad: 'dim' was attached to the lantern group as a whole -- saying the group is dim -- instead of distributing to each lantern, which is what the instruction set requires of a descriptive modifier on a plural. Sentence 2 already says they burned dimly, so the modifier here is pure re-description: 'The lanterns gave weak mist-light.' loses no content and removes the defect.
good. the weak mist-light is tied back to sentence 3, the handful of nightmoths is recorded as a vague count with no number invented, and the attracting carries both participants.

mixed: the count itself lands (twelve nightmoths, at the Middle Row, that night), but bare 'Keepers' again gives no way to tell whether these are sentence 1's keepers -- the parse built a second, unrelated group. Write 'The keepers counted twelve nightmoths at the Middle Row that night.' if it is the same crew.
good. the thread harvest is typed and placed at the Middle Row, and the fall is recorded as a change on it with no figure invented.
good. Pell and Coraline Ash each get their own collecting of the one shared handful of threads, and 'the next morning' resolves to day 18 of Year 1 and is ordered after the previous night's count.

good. Hesper, the threads, the sea-water, the Cauldron Hall venue and the day all land; the one objection raised against it -- sea-water recorded as a place beside the venue -- was overruled, since nothing in the instruction set separates a medium from a venue.

bad: 'the cauldrons' is a first mention with nothing in the text to attach it to, so the parse inferred that they stand in Cauldron Hall -- a location no sentence states. Say it outright and the guess becomes a stated fact: 'The cauldrons at Cauldron Hall yielded two vessels of mire-essence.'

mixed: the earlier yield and its ordering before sentence 9's yield both land, but 'on day 1' carries no year -- the parse records a bare day number with nothing tying it to Year 1. Write 'The cauldrons had yielded three vessels of mire-essence on day 1 of Year 1.' if that is the year you mean.
